input.strategy_title: Audit logging for model inference traffic
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Financial-services customers cannot pass compliance reviews because inference
traffic on RHOAI leaves no audit trail: there is no record of who invoked which
model endpoint, when, and with what outcome. Auditors require tamper-evident,
structured audit events for every inference request. Without this, two
strategic renewals are at risk this fiscal year.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits an audit event capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status (not payloads). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Audit events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics and are not lost on component restart. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Administrators can enable/disable inference auditing per project from the Dashboard. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | A common audit event schema is defined and published so future components (pipelines, workbenches) emit compatible events. Note: the schema in this item is the format HLR-1's events must conform to — HLR-1 cannot ship before the schema is settled. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Documentation covers enabling auditing and interpreting events. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- Auditing of non-inference traffic (pipeline runs, notebook activity) — future
  strategies will adopt the HLR-4 schema
- Long-term audit storage and retention tooling (customer-provided)

## Open Questions

None — the audit sink interface is the standard cluster logging forwarder.

# Define and publish the common inference audit event schema and per-project enablement contract

## Description

This epic produces the shared contract that all inference auditing work builds against: a common audit event schema covering the fields auditors require, plus the definition of how per-project audit enablement is represented so the serving path and the Dashboard build against one contract rather than inventing separate surfaces. The schema is published so that future components (pipelines, workbenches) can emit compatible events.

## Scope

- Define the audit event schema capturing, for every inference request: caller identity, model and version, timestamp, and response status. Payload content is explicitly excluded from the schema.
- Define the per-project audit enablement contract: how the enabled/disabled state for inference auditing is represented per project, so the inference audit emission path and the Dashboard administration control both build against the same interface. The specific mechanism remains an implementation decision for the serving team.
- Publish the schema in the location the serving team designates so future components can consume and conform to it.
- Ensure the schema is structured (machine-parseable) and tamper-evident event content is representable, consistent with the compliance driver in the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A schema document exists that defines a representation for caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status, and explicitly excludes request/response payloads.
- The per-project enablement contract is documented precisely enough that the emission implementation and the Dashboard control can be built against it without further design negotiation.
- The schema is published and versioned in an accessible location for downstream components.
- The schema has been reviewed and agreed by the serving team, with the review outcome recorded.
- The recorded schema review confirms that tamper-evident event content is representable: the schema's structured, machine-parseable records of caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status are suitable for delivery to an append-only, tamper-evident audit sink, satisfying the compliance requirement in the strategy's problem statement.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): A common audit event schema is defined and published so future components emit compatible events. This epic also unblocks HLR-1, which requires events to conform to this schema.

# Emit audit events for KServe inference requests with reliable at-least-once delivery

## Description

This epic implements inference audit logging in the KServe serving stack: every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits a structured audit event conforming to the published common audit event schema, and events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics that survive component restarts.

## Scope

- Emit one audit event per inference request through a KServe endpoint, capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status per the common audit event schema. No request or response payloads are recorded.
- Deliver audit events to the cluster audit sink (the standard cluster logging forwarder) with at-least-once semantics.
- Buffer or otherwise persist in-flight audit events so they are not lost when the emitting component restarts.
- Honor the per-project audit enablement contract: inference auditing emits events only for projects where it is enabled.
- Apply to both serverless and raw deployment modes of InferenceService, consistent with the platform's serving architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For a sample of inference requests against a KServe endpoint, each request produces an audit event containing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status, conforming to the published schema, with no payload data present in the event.
- With auditing enabled for a project, killing and restarting the emitting component mid-traffic results in no audit event loss (at-least-once delivery verified by comparing emitted requests against events received at the cluster audit sink).
- With auditing disabled for a project via the enablement contract, inference requests in that project produce no audit events; with it enabled, they do.
- Events arrive at the standard cluster logging forwarder and are structured (machine-parseable) per the schema.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits an audit event capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status (not payloads).
- HLR-2 (P0): Audit events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics and are not lost on component restart.

## Risks / Notes

- Delivery validation assumes the cluster audit sink (standard cluster logging forwarder) is available in the target cluster; if absent, HLR-2 validation cannot complete. This is an environment prerequisite, not a deliverable of this epic.

# Dashboard administration control for per-project inference auditing

## Description

This epic adds an administration control to the RHOAI Dashboard that allows administrators to enable and disable inference auditing per project, writing the per-project enablement state through the contract defined alongside the common audit event schema.

## Scope

- Add a per-project administration control in the Dashboard for enabling/disabling inference auditing, following existing Dashboard patterns for project-scoped settings.
- Read and write the per-project audit enablement state through the agreed enablement contract (the Dashboard reads and writes cluster resources; it owns no data plane).
- Restrict the control to administrators, consistent with Dashboard authentication and project-scoped RBAC.
- Surface the current auditing state for the project in the control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable and disable inference auditing for a project from the Dashboard, and the state is persisted and reflected when the view is reloaded.
- The written state conforms to the per-project enablement contract and is observable by the inference audit emission path.
- A non-administrative user cannot change the per-project auditing setting.
- The control follows existing Dashboard conventions for project-scoped administration settings.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Administrators can enable/disable inference auditing per project from the Dashboard.

# Document enabling inference auditing and interpreting audit events

## Description

This epic authors end-user documentation for inference audit logging: how administrators enable and disable auditing per project, and how auditors and operators interpret the emitted audit events.

## Scope

- New documentation topic covering enabling and disabling inference auditing per project from the Dashboard, including administrator prerequisites.
- New documentation topic covering the audit event schema: the fields emitted (caller identity, model/version, timestamp, response status), how events reach the cluster audit sink, and how to interpret them for compliance review.
- Cross-references from the model serving documentation to the auditing topics where administrators will look for them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation walks through enabling and disabling per-project inference auditing from the Dashboard, accurate to the implemented behavior.
- Published documentation explains each audit event field and how to retrieve and interpret events from the cluster audit sink.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented emission and Dashboard behavior, with the review outcome recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): Documentation covers enabling auditing and interpreting events.
